title: send has no failure detection for network appliances — fail_on_nonzero is POSIX-shell-only
existing_state: The only built-in way to make a 'send' step fail on command error is fail_on_nonzero, which rewrites the command as eval '<cmd>'; __ssh_helper_send_status=$?; printf '\n<sentinel>:%s\n' ... (Services/Scripting/Commands/SendCommand.cs:134-138) and regex-extracts the status afterwards (:89-100, 140-167). That mechanism only works on POSIX shells; on FortiGate/Cisco/Juniper CLIs — and FortiGate is literally the only parse format the tool ships (ParserFactory.cs:14-15) — it sends garbage commands to the device. There is no pattern-based alternative: to catch '% Invalid input detected' or 'Command fail.' the user must add capture + a separate if/contains step after every single send. Validation only rejects fail_on_nonzero combined with expect (:41-47); combined with respond it is silently allowed.
recommendation: Add fail_pattern (and optionally success_pattern) regex options to the send step, evaluated against the echo/prompt-stripped output (after :86-87) exactly where the existing post-execution fail_on_nonzero check runs (:89-100), routed through the same ApplyOnError path so on_error: continue works. Validate mutual exclusivity with fail_on_nonzero, and also reject fail_on_nonzero+respond. Per Development Guideline 8, surface the new field in the Flow Canvas send block properties and the YAML autocomplete.
user_benefit: One line per step ('fail_pattern: "% Invalid|Command fail"') replaces a capture+if+exit triplet after every device command — the difference between a 10-step and a 30-step script when pushing config to appliances, and errors stop slipping through unnoticed mid-fleet.

evidence.note: eval/printf sentinel wrapper; post-exec status check (natural insertion point); only expect is validated against fail_on_nonzero
FortiGate is the flagship device family — exactly where fail_on_nonzero cannot work
